open_obligations: Note the small 7B-to-14B gap, which Lang et al. list as a limitation.
Check that AnthropicHH as binary classification is comparable to Burns et al.'s ChatGPT reward modeling task.
Check that baselines were reimplemented faithfully on Qwen models.
out.other_title: No weak-to-strong method works consistently; reward modeling gap far from recovered
out.rationale: Burns et al. state none of their methods work consistently and the reward modeling gap is far from recovered. Lang, Huang and Li report their debate-ensemble method raises PGR over finetuning with auxiliary confidence loss on all four tasks, e.g. CosmosQA 17.4% to 56.5% and AnthropicHH 35.0% to 70.0%; models are Qwen-7B and Qwen-14B, a small compute gap.
out.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether weak-to-strong methods can recover more of the performance gap, for debate-augmented weak supervisors on NLP classification

text: The paper reports that its approach (with debate ensembles) outperforms every strong-student baseline on all four tasks, raising PGR relative to Finetune with auxiliary confidence loss from 41.2% to 76.5% on SciQ, 56.4% to 69.2% on BoolQ, 17.4% to 56.5% on CosmosQA and 35.0% to 70.0% on AnthropicHH, with the best test accuracy among strong students.
title: Debate-augmented weak supervisor raises PGR over Burns et al. baselines on four tasks
